Definition: from G243 and G5443; foreign, i.e. (specially) Gentile:--one of another nation.
BiblicalUsage: Once, when Peter explains himself to Cornelius: Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean. The word is the foreigner, the man of another tribe, and the sentence that breaks the wall down.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a foreigner carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the vision behind it, that God showed Peter the sheet from heaven so the gospel could cross into a Gentile house.
